title: MetOp-SG-B1 weather satellite begins launch preparations in French Guiana
excerpt: The satellite has been moved to a cleanroom at Europe’s Spaceport following its arrival from France.
bodyHtml:
The European Space Agency announced on November 4, 2026, that the MetOp Second Generation-B1 weather satellite has been transferred to a cleanroom at Europe’s Spaceport in French Guiana. The satellite was removed from its transport container after being held in storage upon its arrival on October 16.

The satellite arrived in Kourou after departing Bordeaux, France, on October 6 aboard the transport vessel Canopée. The vessel uses an innovative sail system to help reduce fuel consumption and associated carbon dioxide emissions during transport.

Teams are now beginning the final checks and preparations for the satellite. The launch campaign will progress through a series of key milestones, including switching on the satellite, final checks and fuelling. MetOp-SG-B1 will then be encapsulated within the fairing of its Ariane 6 launcher before being transported to the launch pad for liftoff, planned towards the end of the year.
